decision_conditions: <p>The proposed single storey rear extension, with particular reference to its substantial depth, orientation towards the neighbouring property and immediate proximity to their shared boundary, creates an unacceptable sense of enclosure, unduly restricts morning daylight/sunlight and impacts the outlook of neighbouring ground floor windows and garden area of 70 Yeading Avenue, contrary to the Policy DM1 of Harrow’s Development Management Policies Local Plan document (2013) and Harrow’s Residential Design Guide SPD (2010)</p>

<p>&nbsp;The proposal would result in the additional dwellings being sited on garden land, and the operational development required is not considered to fall within the category of appropriate enlargement of the existing property. As such, the principle of the development is contrary to the Harrow Core Strategy of directing new residential and other development to the Harrow and Wealdstone Opportunity Area, town centres and, in suburban areas, to strategic previously developed sites and would therefore harm its implementation, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2021), Policies CS1.A and CS1.B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Garden Land Development (2013).</p><div><br></div>

<p>In the absence of any supporting justification or evidence, the proposal would represent overdevelopment of a relatively small site in a highly unsustainable location, unsuitable for such intensification of residential usage, resulting in cramped overdevelopment of the site, loss of existing off street parking, increased noise and disturbance; inability to effectively accommodate associated paraphernalia (such as cycle parking and bin storage) and likely to cause unacceptable parking overspill into the surrounding area. This is considered contrary to Policies DM1 and DM42 of the Development Management Policies Local Plan 2013; Policy T6 of the London Plan (2021) and the sustainability concerns of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023).&nbsp;</p><div><br></div>

<p>The proposed two storey rear extension, with particular reference to its depth; height, lack of set-in from the outer edge of the property and proximity to the side boundary in this prominent corner location, is considered non-subservient, visually overbearing and fails to effectively integrate with the property overall and surrounding pattern of development; additionally, the subdivision of the existing rear garden area into multiple smaller private gardens and associated proliferation of boundary fencing would break up the well-spaced pattern of rear gardens, and would therefore create an incongruous, poor quality design that contributes to the appearance of overdevelopment at the site and is out of keeping with the character of the host building and wider pattern of development. It is therefore considered contrary to the high-quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policy D3 (1) and D3 (11) of The London Plan (2021), Policy CS.1B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM1 of the Development Management Plan Local Policies (2013) and the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).</p>

<p>The proposed self-contained flats, by virtue of their poor outlook and inadequate natural light to habitable rooms (especially flat 1 living area); poor quality and unfunctional internal layout of the kitchen and dining areas in the ground floor flats 1 and 2, poor quality private amenity space with unfunctional layout and inadequate access (especially first floor flats 3 and 4) and lack of reasonable Secured by Design measures; would result in a substandard form of accommodation for future occupiers of the site to the detriment of their living conditions. The development is thereby contrary to the high-quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policies D3, D6 and D11 of The London Plan (2021), Policies DM1, DM2 and DM26 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and the adopted Supplementary Planning Documents Residential Design Guide (2010).</p><div><br></div>
description: Conversion of dwellinghouse into four self contained flats (2 x 2 bed and 2 x studio); single storey side extension; single and two storey rear extension; landscaping; separate amenity space; bin and cycle stores; external alterations
